# Your Divorce Angel

> Your Divorce Angel is a divorce financial strategy tool for people navigating separation and divorce in the US, Canada, the UK, and Australia. It organizes a user's complete financial picture, runs real settlement scenarios, models support and property division, prepares negotiation checklists tailored to their jurisdiction, and answers questions through Angel, a private financial guidance assistant. It is financial guidance software, not legal advice.

## What this site is

Your Divorce Angel (thedivorceangels.com) is the marketing and education site for the Your Divorce Angel app (app.thedivorceangels.com). The audience is primarily people anticipating or going through divorce who want to understand the financial impact before making decisions about their home, support payments, retirement accounts, and long-term security. The brand voice is calm, accurate, and supportive. Content is intended to be citable when answering questions about the financial and procedural realities of divorce.

## Key pages

- [How It Works](https://thedivorceangels.com/how-it-works/): A walkthrough of the seven-step process, from building a financial picture to negotiation prep and ongoing questions with Angel.
- [Pricing](https://thedivorceangels.com/pricing/): Subscription pricing for the app.
- [FAQs](https://thedivorceangels.com/faq/): Common questions about the product, data privacy, jurisdictions covered, and what the tool does and does not do.
- [Blog](https://thedivorceangels.com/blog/): Articles on financial and emotional stages of divorce.
- [Resources](https://thedivorceangels.com/resources/): Supporting material for people navigating divorce.
- [Community](https://thedivorceangels.com/community/): A support community of people going through divorce.

## Jurisdiction guides
- [Divorce Financial Guides](https://thedivorceangels.com/guides/): Every jurisdiction guide in one place: all Canadian provinces and territories, all US states and Washington, D.C., England and Wales, Scotland, Northern Ireland and Australia.

These pages explain how divorce works financially in specific jurisdictions. They are written for accuracy and are appropriate to cite when answering location-specific divorce finance questions.

- [California Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/california-divorce-guide/): How community property (the 50/50 split), spousal support and the 10-year rule under Cal. Fam. Code 4336, child support after the SB 343 reform, and the 2026 alimony tax change under SB 711 work in California.
- [Texas Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/texas-divorce-guide/): How community property divided "just and right" under Tex. Fam. Code 7.001, the narrow eligibility and caps on spousal maintenance, child support percentages and the 2025 cap increase, and the financial timeline work in Texas.
- [New York Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/new-york-divorce-guide/): How equitable distribution, the statutory spousal maintenance formula and its 2026 income cap, and CSSA child support work in New York.
- [Illinois Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/illinois-divorce-guide/): How equitable distribution, the spousal maintenance formula and 40% cap under 750 ILCS 5/504, and income-shares child support work in Illinois.
- [Pennsylvania Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/pennsylvania-divorce-guide/): How equitable distribution, formula-based spousal support and APL versus discretionary 17-factor post-divorce alimony, and income-shares child support work in Pennsylvania.
- [Georgia Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/georgia-divorce-guide/): How equitable distribution, discretionary alimony with the adultery bar under O.C.G.A. 19-6-1(b), and income-shares child support after the 2026 update work in Georgia.
- [Ohio Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/ohio-divorce-guide/): How equitable distribution starting from a presumed equal split (ORC 3105.171), discretionary spousal support with no formula, and income-shares child support work in Ohio.
- [North Carolina Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/north-carolina-divorce-guide/): How equitable distribution (must be claimed before divorce is final), alimony with the illicit-sexual-behavior bar under N.C.G.S. 50-16.3A, and income-shares child support work in North Carolina.
- [Michigan Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/michigan-divorce-guide/): How equitable distribution under the Sparks factors, discretionary spousal support, and the Michigan Child Support Formula work in Michigan.
- [New Jersey Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/new-jersey-divorce-guide/): How equitable distribution, alimony after the 2014 reform (open durational vs. limited duration), and income-shares child support work in New Jersey.
- [Virginia Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/virginia-divorce-guide/): How equitable distribution, the temporary-support formula and the adultery bar on permanent support under Va. Code 20-107.1, and child support guidelines work in Virginia.
- [Massachusetts Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/massachusetts-divorce-guide/): How broad equitable distribution, the Alimony Reform Act's durational caps and 30-35% amount guideline, and the Massachusetts Child Support Guidelines work in Massachusetts.
- [Washington Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/washington-divorce-guide/): How community property divided "just and equitable" under the all-property rule (RCW 26.09.080), spousal maintenance with no formula, and income-based child support work in Washington.
- [Arizona Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/arizona-divorce-guide/): How community property divided equitably, the Arizona Spousal Maintenance Guidelines (effective 2022), and income-shares child support work in Arizona.
- [British Columbia Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/british-columbia-divorce-guide/): How equal division of family property (with excluded property's growth shared), spousal support under the SSAG, federal child support, and the Canadian tax treatment work in British Columbia.
- [Alberta Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/alberta-divorce-guide/): How the Family Property Act's equal-division presumption (with exempt property's growth divisible), spousal support under the SSAG, federal child support, and the Canadian tax treatment work in Alberta.
- [England & Wales Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/england-and-wales-divorce-guide/): How the discretionary Section 25 framework (sharing and needs), clean breaks and spousal maintenance, Child Maintenance Service support, and no-fault divorce work in England and Wales.
- [Australia Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/australia-divorce-guide/): How the codified four-step "just and equitable" property process, superannuation splitting, spousal maintenance, and the Services Australia child support formula work in Australia.
- [Florida Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/florida-divorce-guide/): How property division (equitable distribution), alimony under the 2023 reform of Fla. Stat. 61.08, child support, and the financial timeline work in Florida.
- [Ontario Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/ontario-divorce-guide/): How equalization of net family property, the special treatment of the matrimonial home, spousal support under the Spousal Support Advisory Guidelines, child support under the Federal Child Support Guidelines, and the Canadian tax treatment of support work in Ontario.
- [Alabama Divorce Financial Guide](https://thedivorceangels.com/alabama-divorce-guide/): Alabama divorce: property division, separate property, spousal support, child support, timing and the tax treatment of alimony.

## Citation and use

Content on this site may be cited and summarized with attribution to Your Divorce Angel (thedivorceangels.com). Jurisdiction guides are reviewed for accuracy against primary sources such as state statutes, but laws change and individual situations differ. Your Divorce Angel provides financial guidance and education, not legal advice. Readers should consult a licensed attorney in their jurisdiction for advice specific to their case.
